The task defines what an output means: filling a missing RNA value from an image, estimating a drug response and predicting a gene-disruption response are different tasks, and success at one does not validate another. evidence.supportingExcerpt: Mass spectrometry-based proteomics can identify and increasingly quantify thousands of proteins in complex samples (Aebersold and Mann, 2003). Protein inference, working out which proteins are present from the identified peptides, is difficult because many peptide sequences occur in several proteins (Lukasse and America, 2014). The target-decoy strategy uses hits to a decoy database to distinguish correct from incorrect peptide identifications (Elias and Gygi, 2007), and a dataset-level false-positive rate is a property of the accepted set, not a guarantee for each identification (Beausoleil and colleagues, 2006 reported a peptide false-positive rate of 1.3 per cent for their dataset). In 105 genomically annotated breast cancers, 77 of which gave high-quality data, pathway analysis of the phosphoproteome identified a G-protein-coupled receptor cluster that was not readily identified at the mRNA level (Mertins and colleagues, 2016).

Reading guide (OnCo inference built on the sources). Bottom-up proteomics digests proteins to peptides, separates them by liquid chromatography, measures ions and fragments by tandem mass spectrometry, and identifies peptides by software, so evidence for an intact, functional protein is indirect. A shared peptide cannot choose between candidate proteins; inference uses the other peptides recovered and reports ambiguity. A ratio needs its denominator, an absolute amount needs calibration with standards in a matched matrix (Carr and colleagues, 2014), and a peptide standard does not by itself show recovery of the original protein. A bulk extract mixes cells and loses their positions, so a peptide signal per mass of extract is not receptors per cancer cell.

A 2025 benchmark found that none of five single-cell foundation models and two other deep-learning models predicted transcriptome changes after single or double gene perturbations better than deliberately simple baselines; for most genes the predictions of scGPT, UCE and scBERT did not vary across perturbations, and those of GEARS and scFoundation varied considerably less than the observed values (Ahlmann-Eltze and colleagues, 2025). Reading guide (OnCo inference). The task defines what an output means: filling a missing RNA value from an image, estimating a drug response and predicting a gene-disruption response are different tasks, and success at one does not validate another. A virtual perturbation changes a model input and calculates an output; it is not a performed experiment, and masking a gene value is not the same as removing the gene's function. Predicted RNA is not measured RNA, protein activity or patient benefit. Agreement summarised across all genes can conceal poor prediction of the few genes that changed, so compare against simple baselines on the genes that moved. An association learned from untreated tissue does not by itself identify a causal drug effect. Whether a model's output supports treatment selection needs separate intended-use clinical evidence, whereas prioritising experiments is a lesser claim.

evidence.supportingExcerpt: Mesmer was trained on TissueNet, a dataset of more than 1 million manually labelled cells, and was reported to generalise across the tissue types and imaging platforms in that dataset at human-level performance; its authors note that segmentation inaccuracies can substantially bias the identification and counting of cells, and that cells whose nucleus lies outside the imaging plane are missed by nucleus-based methods (Greenwald and colleagues, 2022). In that evaluation, a predicted and a true cell with a one-to-one match by intersection over union count as accurate, predicted cells with no match are false positives and true cells with no match are false negatives. The Cellpose study reported a generalist method trained on more than 70,000 segmented objects that worked without retraining across the image types it evaluated (Stringer and colleagues, 2021). Baysor was developed because methods that approximate cell positions from nuclear stains make cell boundaries hard to distinguish in single-molecule spatial data (Petukhov and colleagues, 2022).

Reading guide (definitions plus OnCo inference). Detection asks whether a cell was found, segmentation asks which pixels belong to it, and phenotyping classifies the cell afterwards; finding a nucleus does not give a reliable whole-cell boundary. Intersection over union is the area two masks share divided by the area either covers, from 0 to 1, and a single value can hide missed or merged cells, so check object counts and characteristic errors too. A mask assigns existing signals to estimated regions and is not a measurement of a new marker. Merging, splitting and missing cells distort counts, marker combinations and spatial relations, so overlay masks on the original channels.

evidence.supportingExcerpt: Reading guide (OnCo inference built on the definitions above): a test-guided strategy is the test, its result rule, the action taken and the care setting taken together, and its utility is judged against a defined alternative using outcomes and harms. Measurement evidence (repeat readings of a spiked target), meaning evidence (a result followed by a later outcome) and use evidence (the strategy compared with an alternative) are three separate questions, and an answer to one is not an answer to another.

Evidence table in words. Does it measure correctly? Inspect reference specimens, repeats, background, input range and failures; the tempting overread is that reliable measurement must predict benefit. Does the result mean something clinically? Inspect an appropriate population, endpoint, follow-up and independent validation; the tempting overread is that association means the proposed intervention works. Does acting on it help? Inspect a defined decision strategy against a comparator with meaningful outcomes and harms; the tempting overread is that a changed decision must be improved care.
